subject: Multi-year prepay: true-up mechanics and ramp schedule clarifications
messages:
From: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@fintech.co>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring multi-year prepay + true-up approach

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stellar is keen to move from a pilot into a committed prepay. Before we loop in procurement, a couple quick commercial questions so we can model TCO: 

1) For a 3-year prepay with an annual invoicing cadence, how do you typically structure the term discount vs. an annual-only prepay?
2) We have a projected growth ramp: Year 1 = 30% of committed, Year 2 = 75%, Year 3 = 120% (we expect to over-index as product usage grows). Do you allow multi-year ramp windows or do you enforce per-year true-ups?
3) True-up mechanics: do you do a single end-of-term reconciliation across the full multi-year commitment, or per-12-month true-ups? Is there a buffer band we can apply to avoid frequent overage billing?

Attaching a high-level usage projection. Looking for the simplest approach that gives us predictability without penalizing typical adoption cliffs.

Best,
Rajesh
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Fintech Co

Attachment: Stellar_usage_projection_Q3-4.xlsx (spreadsheet, 82KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@fintech.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay + true-up approach

Rajesh —

Thanks for the projection and the clear questions. Quick answers up-front, then a suggested approach below: 

TL;DR
- We can offer a stepped term discount for a 3-year prepay (bigger discount for multi-year commit vs annual-only).
- We support per-year true-ups by default, but can agree to an end-of-term reconciliation for a multi-year contract if you prefer a single annual invoice cadence with a final true-up in year 3.
- We can add a buffer band (typical range 10–20%) to reduce overage noise; for your ramp profile I’d propose a 15% buffer on annual usage.

Suggested structure (based on your projections):
- Commitment: $X prepay across 3 years (we'll translate to token/embedding units once we finalize model mix).
- Yearly invoicing; per-year forecast for SOW/finance purposes.
- True-up options (choose one):
  a) Annual true-up: reconcile actual vs committed at each 12-month anniversary; overages billed monthly/quarterly.
  b) End-of-term true-up (single reconciliation): we invoice annually for the prepay; at the end of year 3 we reconcile cumulative usage vs cumulative commit and apply a single true-up.
- Buffer band: set at 15% by default for end-of-term option (so Stellar only pays overage if cumulative usage exceeds committed + 15% buffer).
- Ramp allowance: we can allow Year 1 usage to be as low as 50% of the Year 1 projected commit without penalty if you choose the end-of-term reconciliation.

I'll attach a clean term sheet with placeholders for dollar amounts and the buffer band. Marissa — can you confirm commercial discounts for the above (we discussed a 12% blended discount for 3-year multi-pay)? Aisha — any concerns from billing/collections on the end-of-term true-up?

Next steps:
- We can hop on a short call to lock these choices; otherwise we can capture the option in the term sheet and run through procurement.

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: Stellar_PrePay_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Rajesh Patel <r.patel@fintech.co>
Cc: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay + true-up approach

Rajesh / Karthik —

I ran the numbers on the proposed 3-year structure. A couple clarifications and one proposal to keep procurement simple: 

Clarifications: 
- When we say "committed units" we'll define it in the SOW as token-equivalent units per year (we'll map to model/embedding mix at contract signature).
- Buffer band application: for end-of-term true-up we apply the buffer to the cumulative committed units (i.e., committed_total * 1.15).

Commercial proposal: 
- 3-year prepay, paid annually. Blended discount of 12% off list across the three years (we can tier the discount if you want larger savings front-loaded).
- End-of-term true-up with a 15% buffer band. If cumulative usage <= committed_total + 15% -> no additional charge. If cumulative usage > committed_total + 15% -> true-up charges applied to the delta at standard overage rate with a 30-day invoicing term.
- Ramp protection: Year 1 usage can be as low as 50% of Year 1 committed units without re-pricing; shortfall in Year 1 counts toward the cumulative total for the final reconciliation.

Pros/cons: end-of-term reduces noise and is easier for your finance team; downside for Redwood is higher tail risk if usage significantly exceeds projections early, but the 15% buffer mitigates that.

If this aligns, we'll insert the language into the term sheet and circulate to your procurement/legal.

—Marissa
Head of Deals | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@fintech.co>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, Emma Zhou <emma@stellarai.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 07:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay + true-up approach

Karthik / Marissa —

Appreciate the clarity. A couple follow-ups from our side: 

1) Buffer band: is 15% negotiable? Given our Year 3 expectation of 120% usage, we'd prefer a 20% buffer if we can get a commensurate increase in discount (even 1–2% additional).
2) Overages: can you confirm whether overage rates are billed at list or a discounted overage rate? In enterprise deals we've seen vendors offer a reduced overage % for multi-year customers.
3) Migration & model mix: if we move 60% of our calls in Year 2 to a cheaper embedding-dominant model, can that change how units map to committed dollars? We want the contract to avoid per-model re-pricing mid-term.

If you can outline answers in the term sheet (or mark up the PDF), we'll share with procurement next week.

Thanks — Rajesh

On Thu, May 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rajesh — noted — I'll propose two variant lines in the term sheet: 15% buffer (12% blended discount) and 20% buffer (14% blended discount).
> Overages will be billed at a lower overage rate for multi-year customers (we'll show both in the sheet).
> We'll add a model-mix clause: unit mapping is set at signature and re-mapping requires mutual agreement (we'll include a small re-mapping review window at each 12-month anniversary).
> K

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@fintech.co>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-year prepay + true-up approach

Rajesh —

Following internal billing review and Marissa's commercial options, we can confirm the following final language to insert in the term sheet for procurement review: 

1) Buffer band options (pick one):
   - Option A: 15% buffer band; Blended discount = 12%
   - Option B: 20% buffer band; Blended discount = 14%

2) True-up mechanics: end-of-term reconciliation applies to cumulative committed units across the 3-year term. If cumulative usage <= committed_total + buffer_band -> no additional charges. If cumulative usage > committed_total + buffer_band -> customer pays overage on the delta at the agreed overage rate.

3) Overage rate: multi-year customers receive a discounted overage rate = list_overage_rate * 0.85 (i.e., 15% off list).

4) Model/mix clause: unit mapping to $ is set at signature. Parties will review model mix at each 12-month anniversary and may agree to re-map units by mutual written consent; unilateral re-pricing is not permitted.

5) Invoicing & payment: annual invoices, 30-day payment terms; true-up invoiced within 30 days of reconciliation with 30-day payment term.

Next step: Karthik and Marissa will attach the marked-up term sheet (two-line option) and we can schedule a procurement call for next Wednesday at 10am PT if that works for your team.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Manager, Billing & Contracts | Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
